packs.title: Inlet, Arts and Stories
packs.promise: Explore Atlantic City through waterfront, art, heritage and civic outings.

q.s: Trace how a public waterfront edge separates visitor space from the basin.
st: From a safe open path, or the city's project account, locate the public seawall and visitor-side path.
Notice or identify one feature that guides people and one feature that meets the water edge.
Draw a simple section view keeping visitors on the public side of the barrier.

q.s: Read one current Noyes gallery work with its credited maker and material.
st: Choose a work in an open Noyes gallery or on its current exhibition page.
Record the artist credit and one material, technique or form shown by the operator.
Write one observed feature and one interpretation in separate lines; do not confuse them.

q.s: Read an arrival station's public wayfinding without buying a ticket.
st: Locate the terminal's public entrance and one accessible or transfer facility on NJ Transit's station page.
Find how a traveler would identify a legal exit toward the city without entering a platform.
Sketch a two-step arrival plan and name the official source for each step.

packs.title: Boardwalk to Steel Pier
packs.promise: Walk central Atlantic City through public history, art and shore places.

q.s: Read the scale of Boardwalk Hall from its public exterior and operator history.
st: From an open public approach or operator exterior image, choose one feature that signals a large gathering building.
Read the venue's history and identify its original civic purpose.
Make a two-part note separating the visible exterior feature from the documented purpose.

q.s: Read a restored public mural through its artist's credit and visible additions.
st: Locate the mural from a safe public sidewalk or the Arts Foundation's 2025 images.
Credit artist Denton Burrows and identify one color or birdlife detail the Foundation says was added in restoration.
Write one observation and one sourced restoration fact as separate statements.

q.s: Connect a library's public service with a wayfinding feature.
st: Choose one public library service from the current branch page, such as computers or reading space.
Identify an entrance, sign or published layout cue that helps a visitor find the service.
Write a short access note using the library's current hours and address.
